project_name: Synergy Data Center & Services Baker City facility
developer: Synergy Data Center & Services / Chaves Consulting / Arikkan Inc.
status_detail: Local commercial colocation/hosting facility in Baker City; 2010 launch article described Phase I at Baker Tower, and current Baker Tower/Chaves pages still list Synergy as operating a Tier 2+/Tier 3+ facility.
notes: Not a hyperscale project; small regional data hosting/colocation facility. Address is inconsistently reported by trackers as 1650 Dewey Ave while Baker Tower pages identify 1705 Main St/Baker Tower tenancy.

status_detail: No reliable county/EDA/news evidence found for an operating, planned, approved, or rejected commercial data center project in Benton County during quick county-level exploration.
notes: Search hits were government internal IT/data center operations, Corvallis enterprise-zone information, generic vendor pages, and social discussion about comprehensive-plan concerns; no named project or application found.

status_detail: OPB reported state/county officials are aware of one data center in Clackamas County, operated by Siemens on its Wilsonville campus; county officials said no future land-use applications had been received.
notes: Facility appears to be a corporate/private campus data center, not a county-jurisdiction hyperscale development. Clackamas County was considering policy/moratorium discussions in 2026, with no pending future applications reported.

project_name: Agile Design North Coast Business Park data center
aliases: Warrenton data center and technology incubator
status_detail: Clatsop County commissioners rejected a proposed purchase agreement after repeated extensions for a proposed data center and technology incubator at the county-owned North Coast Business Park.
notes: News reports identify 67 acres in due diligence at North Coast Business Park and a related tech-incubator concept; proposal collapsed/rejected before construction.

status_detail: No official plan, application, or named operating data center project found for Columbia County.
notes: Local article framed data centers as a possibility but reported resource constraints and no official plans yet. County-site search hits were internal county IT/data-center discussions, not commercial data center projects.

status_detail: No reliable official or local-news evidence found for a named commercial data center project in Coos County.
notes: County search hits included zoning/traffic examples using 'data center' or 'server farm' as generic land-use terms and generic vendor service pages. A recent Facebook claim about an AI data center in Bandon was not supported by official/local-news evidence in this pass, so it is not recorded as a project.

status_detail: Meta announced continued expansion in 2021: two new buildings, 900,000 additional square feet, and an 11-building campus totaling nearly 4.6 million square feet and over $2 billion investment once completed.
notes: EDCO describes Prineville as home to Meta and Apple Fortune 50 data centers and says Meta's campus is its flagship/largest in its fleet. Capacity not stated in official source.

status_detail: EDCO identifies Prineville as home to Apple and Meta Fortune 50 data centers; OPB reported Apple followed Facebook in Prineville in 2012 and that ongoing construction would leave Prineville with six data centers at that time.
notes: County/city economic development material confirms Apple data-center presence but does not give MW capacity in accessible pages reviewed.

developer: BendBroadband; later TDS/OneNeck; acquired by US Signal
status_detail: BendBroadband built/opened a 30,000-square-foot data center in Bend for colocation, hosted storage, cloud computing, and managed services; tracker records later ownership via OneNeck and US Signal, with 0.9 MW listed.
notes: USGBC confirms facility/service purpose; Oregon Business reported $16M/30,000 sq ft. MW comes from tracker, not official source.

developer: Fort Rock Data Center / Cascade Divide Partners
status_detail: Fort Rock's site lists an operating Bend data/cloud/colocation facility at 207 SW Columbia St.; DataCenterMap lists Columbia 1 at that address and reports 2 MW.
notes: Capacity from tracker. DCD reported DirectLink and SMTA acquired a majority stake in Cascade Divide's Bend facility in 2023.

project_name: BoxMiner La Pine data center proposal
aliases: La Pine Industrial Park data center
status_detail: La Pine City Council unanimously rejected a proposed data-center land sale on May 27, 2026 after public opposition; proposal was for a 20-acre county-owned parcel in La Pine Industrial Park and an initial roughly 20,000-square-foot facility with 20 MW load reported by local/tracker sources.
notes: Land was described as Deschutes County-owned, requiring final approval from both La Pine City Council and Deschutes County commissioners; city rejection stopped the sale process before county approval/construction.

aliases: Umpqua Technologies Group Roseburg Data Center
status_detail: Data-center trackers list an operational Roseburg/Spruce data center in Douglas County; local reporting on Cascade Divide's Bend expansion said the company already operated a Roseburg data center.
notes: Evidence is weaker than official county records; included because multiple tracker/local-news references identify a Roseburg facility. Elevate Douglas separately says Douglas County is no longer actively recruiting data centers and removed them from its target industry list in 2023.

status_detail: No official, EDA, or local-news evidence found for a commercial data center project in Curry County.
notes: Search results were official economic-development/GIS pages with no data-center project, generic data-center consultant landing pages, and unrelated power/interconnection items.
